c.tagline: Sri Lanka's beach-and-lagoon gateway beside Colombo's airport, built on fishing, Dutch canals, and Catholic churches.

taxi.fareNote: Tuk-tuks and cabs are meant to be metered but drivers often try to negotiate a flat fare; use the PickMe or Uber app to lock in a fair metered price.

emergency.note: Dial 119 for police and 110 or 1990 for ambulance; the Tourist Police hotline in the Colombo area is 011 242 1052.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Petty theft on the beach; drug hustlers — caution at night

hood_desc: The walkable heart of Negombo's tourist strip, a string of guesthouses, seafood cafes, and beach bars just north of the town centre; the easiest base for first-timers and a short tuk-tuk from the airport.

Negombo's main resort and nightlife strip along Browns Beach, lined with beach hotels, spas, dive shops, and open-air bars and clubs; best for travellers who want dining and evenings out steps from the sand.

A quieter beach stretch north of the resort strip, with calmer sands, family guesthouses, and the landmark St. Mary's and St. Sebastian's churches nearby; suits those wanting a relaxed pace close to the water.
The bustling old town around the Dutch fort ruins, the lagoon-side fish market, and the ornate 'Little Rome' Catholic churches; best for sightseeing, local markets, and Sri Lankan street food.
A residential fishing area on the lagoon and Duwa island, laced with the Dutch (Hamilton) canal, mangroves, and outrigger canoes; a calm, local-flavoured base for boat tours and birdwatching.

transit.hours: Trains and buses generally run around 5am-10pm with sparse late-night service; after that, tuk-tuks and rideshare apps are the norm.
transit.note: The Puttalam-line train from Negombo Downtown Station runs south to Colombo Fort and north to Chilaw, bypassing road traffic; frequent buses use the Colombo-Katunayake (E03) Expressway, and metered tuk-tuks booked via PickMe fill the gaps.
transit.pay: Train tickets are bought at station counters; SLTB and private buses are paid in cash to the conductor with small rupee notes. There is no citywide rechargeable transit card.

sys.n: Sri Lanka Railways (Puttalam Line to Colombo)

transit.m: Public bus route 240 to Negombo (~30-40 min)

tip.r: Around 10% at restaurants if a service charge isn't already added; small tips for tuk-tuk drivers and hotel staff are appreciated but not required.

food.name: Negombo Crab Curry
food.desc: Lagoon mud crab cooked in a dark, coconut-thick gravy with roasted spices and pandan, cracked open by hand and mopped up with rice or roti.

places.name: Lords Restaurant and Bar
places.note: Long-running traveller favourite on the beach road, known for seafood and curry platters.

places.name: Lellama Fish Market Eateries
places.note: Buy crab at the working fish market and eat it cooked at the small kitchens nearby.

places.name: Bijou Restaurant
places.note: Swiss-run kitchen of many years standing, dependable seafood and Sri Lankan curries.

food.name: Lagoon Prawns
food.desc: Negombo's famous lagoon prawns, either devilled with onion and chili or in a mild coconut curry, served with red rice and sambols.

places.name: Lellama Fish Market Eateries
places.note: Prawns straight off the outrigger boats; the freshest and cheapest in town.

places.name: Lords Restaurant and Bar
places.note: Reliable devilled prawns and garlic prawns on the main tourist strip.

places.name: Icebear Restaurant
places.note: Long-established Swiss-Sri Lankan guesthouse restaurant near the beach, good seafood plates.

food.name: Kottu Roti
food.desc: Godamba roti chopped on a hot plate with egg, vegetables and chicken or cheese, to a two-blade clatter you can hear from the street.

places.name: Main Street Kottu Stalls
places.note: Evening street kitchens on the main road; follow the sound of the metal blades.

places.name: Sea Street Eateries
places.note: Local short-eat shops doing kottu and rotis from dusk, priced for residents.

places.name: Porutota Road Cafes
places.note: Beach-strip kitchens serving cheese and seafood kottu late into the night.

food.name: Hoppers and String Hoppers
food.desc: Bowl-shaped fermented rice pancakes crisp at the edge, often with an egg in the middle; string hoppers are steamed rice-noodle nests eaten with dhal and sambol.

places.name: Main Street Hopper Stalls
places.note: Early-morning and evening hopper carts; the only times they are made.

places.name: Sea Street Eateries
places.note: Local kades serving string hoppers with dhal, coconut sambol and fish curry.

places.name: Icebear Restaurant
places.note: Sit-down option for a hopper breakfast if you would rather not chase the carts.

food.name: Negombo Fish Curry and Ambul Thiyal
food.desc: Seer fish or tuna in a coconut and chili gravy, or ambul thiyal - fish dry-cooked with goraka until sour, black and firm enough to keep for days.

places.name: Lellama Fish Market Eateries
places.note: The island's biggest fish market after Colombo; pick the fish, have it curried.

places.name: Bijou Restaurant
places.note: Consistent Sri Lankan fish curries alongside a European menu; long-standing favourite.

places.name: Lords Restaurant and Bar
places.note: Rice and curry spreads with several fish preparations at once.

food.name: Lamprais and Rice and Curry
food.desc: Dutch Burgher lamprais bakes rice, meat curry, frikkadel and sambol in a banana leaf; the everyday rice and curry piles five or more dishes on one plate.

places.name: Icebear Restaurant
places.note: Long-running restaurant serving proper rice-and-curry spreads in the old town.

places.name: Main Street Bakeries and Kades
places.note: Town bakeries sell lamprais parcels and short eats, a nod to the Dutch fort heritage.

places.name: Lords Restaurant and Bar
places.note: Full curry platters for visitors who want everything on one table.

food.name: Ceylon Tea and King Coconut
food.desc: Strong, sweet milk tea from the up-country estates, and thambili - orange king coconut cut open at the roadside for its cool water.

places.name: Main Street Tea Kades
places.note: Roadside tea shops pour plain tea and milk tea with short eats all day.

places.name: Lellama Fish Market
places.note: Tea and thambili vendors work the market from before dawn.

places.name: Porutota Road Cafes
places.note: Beach-road cafes serve iced tea and king coconut straight from the pile.

food.name: Coconut Arrack and Toddy
food.desc: Sri Lanka's national spirit, distilled from fermented coconut flower sap; the raw fermented version, toddy, is still tapped along this coast.

places.name: Lords Restaurant and Bar
places.note: Best-known bar on the strip, with arrack cocktails as well as the neat pour.

places.name: Porutota Road Bars
places.note: Row of beach bars for arrack and soda or arrack with ginger beer at sunset.

places.name: Negombo Beach Hotel Bars
places.note: Hotel terraces along the sand pour local arrack brands with a sea view.

landmarks: Negombo Beach
A long stretch of golden sand lined with palm trees and fishing boats, offering classic tropical sunset photography on Sri Lanka's west coast.
Negombo Fish Market (Lellama)
One of Sri Lanka's largest fish markets bursts with color and action at dawn as fishermen haul in the day's catch alongside traditional outrigger boats.
St. Mary's Church
A grand Baroque-style Catholic church with an ornately painted ceiling, reflecting Negombo's nickname 'Little Rome' from its Portuguese colonial heritage.
Negombo Dutch Fort
The weathered ruins and gateway of a 17th-century Dutch fort recall the era when Negombo was a prized center of the cinnamon trade.
Dutch Canal (Hamilton Canal)
A historic waterway built by Dutch colonists still winds through town, lined with palms and used by fishermen much as it was centuries ago.
Angurukaramulla Temple
A vibrant Buddhist temple famous for its giant reclining Buddha statue and elaborately painted halls depicting scenes from Buddhist scripture.
Muthurajawela Marsh
A vast coastal wetland just south of Negombo where boat safaris reveal mangroves, birdlife, and crocodiles in a peaceful natural setting.
Negombo Lagoon
A scenic lagoon dotted with traditional 'oruwa' outrigger canoes and stilt fishermen, best photographed in the soft light of early morning.
Duwa Fishing Village
A colorful working fishing hamlet across the lagoon bridge where brightly painted boats and drying nets create an authentic slice of coastal life.
Negombo Beach Road Fishing Boats
Rows of vividly painted traditional fishing boats pulled up along the shore make for one of the most iconic and photogenic sights in Negombo.

train.note: Negombo station is in the town centre on the Puttalam (northern coastal) line, with slow trains to Colombo Fort taking about 1.5-2 hrs. Services are infrequent and entirely unreserved, so tickets are bought at the window shortly before departure and the bus is usually the quicker option. There is no rail link to Bandaranaike International Airport, which lies about 9 km south and is reached by taxi or town bus. Sri Lanka has no international passenger rail.

bus.note: The main bus stand is beside the lagoon and fish market in the town centre. Buses to Colombo leave roughly every 30 minutes and take 1-1.5 hrs, Kandy services run about every 30 minutes and take 3-4 hrs, and route 240 shuttles to the airport in around 30 minutes. All are pay-on-board with no advance booking, split between state SLTB and private operators; there are no cross-border coaches from Sri Lanka.

ferry.note: Negombo has no scheduled passenger ferry. The lagoon and the old Dutch canal are worked by outrigger fishing craft and tourist boats hired by the hour at the canal bank and the fish market, and the nearest commercial passenger port is Colombo, about 40 km south.

half.name: Colombo
half.blurb: Sri Lanka's commercial capital, with colonial Dutch and British-era buildings around the Galle Face Green oceanfront.

half.name: Chilaw and Munneswaram Temple
half.blurb: A coastal town with one of Sri Lanka's oldest Hindu temple complexes, dedicated to Shiva.

full.name: Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage
full.blurb: A sanctuary and breeding center for orphaned elephants, where herds are walked to the river twice daily for bathing.

full.name: Kandy
full.blurb: A hill-country city centered on the Temple of the Tooth Relic, overlooking an artificial lake.
